answer.answer: The umpire shows/raises a red card when faulting the offending side: either “if previously warned” or “in cases of flagrant offence or breach” (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Law 16.7.1.2–16.7.1.3). Next, on faulting a side the umpire reports the offending side immediately to the Referee, “who shall have the power to disqualify the offending side from the match” (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), Law 16.7.2). If the Referee decides to disqualify, a black card is given to the umpire, who calls “Come here,” then “… [name of player(s)], disqualified for misconduct” with a specific explanation, while raising the right hand holding the black card above the head (ITTO 7.0 (5), Clause 5.17.5). The Referee is also to be called on court for “flagrant or other misbehaviour resulting in a red card (Law 16.7)” (ITTO 7.0 (5), Clause 3.6.2).

answer.answer: In a Para badminton Standing Class, the standard 1.15-metre service height rule does not apply. So in your standing class, you may serve as long as the whole shuttle is below your waist (lowest part of your bottom rib) and your racket shaft and head are pointing downward when you strike it.
